blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Running a procurement operation at the intermediate level is less about individual deals and more about building a system that produces good buying decisions, week after week. The good systems have a few things in common: a clear approved supplier list, negotiated framework agreements for repeat purchases, and a small number of senior buyers who handle the big, strategic suppliers personally.

The mistake most teams make is to treat every purchase as fresh. That is slow, expensive, and inconsistent. A well-run procurement function standardises the ninety per cent of purchases that do not really need a debate, and concentrates its real attention on the ten per cent that do.

Done well, this quietly saves money every week without anyone noticing — which is exactly the sign of good procurement.

items.q: According to the text, what is procurement at the intermediate level mostly about?
options: Reducing the number of suppliers to one
Building a system that produces good buying decisions
items.why: "less about individual deals and more about building a system that produces good buying decisions."

items.q: What mistake do most teams make?
options: They negotiate framework agreements too early
They standardise everything, even complex deals
They treat every purchase as fresh
items.why: "The mistake most teams make is to treat every purchase as fresh."

items.q: How should a well-run function split its attention?
options: Focus only on the cheapest suppliers
Let senior buyers handle all purchases personally
Standardise the routine ninety per cent and focus on the ten per cent that need it
items.why: "standardises the ninety per cent… and concentrates its real attention on the ten per cent that do."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Repeat purchases should each be negotiated from scratch to get the best deal
A small number of senior buyers should handle strategic suppliers
items.why: Inferência: o texto critica exatamente tratar toda compra como nova — negociar do zero é o erro.

items.q: What does "without anyone noticing" suggest about good procurement?
options: It hides its costs from management
It fails to deliver real results
It works so smoothly that its savings go unnoticed
items.why: Inferência: a economia é constante e silenciosa — sinal de um sistema que roda bem, não de descuido.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver revisando como sua equipe de compras mudou de abordagem. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, looking back at this year, I think the team has genuinely turned a corner. Twelve months ago we were negotiating every single repeat purchase from scratch — the same cardboard, the same cleaning contracts, the same freight lanes, over and over. It was exhausting, and honestly it saved us very little.

What we have done since then is build framework agreements with our top five suppliers. We have agreed the terms once, and now the routine orders just flow against those agreements. Nobody has to reopen a negotiation for a box of screws.

The numbers back it up. We have reduced ad-hoc purchasing by roughly sixty per cent, and the buyers have finally got time to work on the strategic accounts that actually move the needle.

I won't pretend it was quick. It has taken most of the year, and there were weeks when it felt like nothing was changing. But we have laid the foundations now, and the pay-off runs for years, not months. Next, I'd like us to look at whether we can bring two more suppliers into the same framework.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What were the team doing twelve months ago?
options: Negotiating every repeat purchase from scratch
items.why: "we were negotiating every single repeat purchase from scratch."

items.q: What has the team built with the top five suppliers?
options: Framework agreements with terms agreed once
items.why: "we have done… build framework agreements with our top five suppliers… agreed the terms once."

items.q: By how much has ad-hoc purchasing been reduced?
items.why: "We have reduced ad-hoc purchasing by roughly sixty per cent."

items.q: What does Oliver imply the buyers can now do with their freed-up time?
options: Work on the strategic accounts that make a real difference
items.why: Inferência: ele liga o tempo liberado às contas estratégicas 'that actually move the needle'.

items.q: How would you best describe Oliver's overall assessment?
options: Uncertain whether the change was worthwhile
Proud of a slow but lasting improvement
Focused only on this month's savings
items.why: Inferência: ele admite que foi lento, mas fala em fundações lançadas e retorno por anos — satisfação com uma melhoria duradoura.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Only vendors on the approved supplier list may receive purchase orders." This list is…
options: a ranking of the cheapest vendors
the set of suppliers cleared to do business with the company
items.why: Approved supplier list = lista de fornecedores aprovados, os que estão liberados para vender à empresa.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Once the ___ is signed, routine orders flow against agreed prices without renegotiation."
items.why: Framework agreement = acordo-quadro: fixa os termos uma vez e os pedidos correm sob ele.

items.q: "Copier paper is a classic repeat purchase." A repeat purchase is…
options: a duplicate order made by mistake
an item bought regularly under the same terms
items.why: Repeat purchase = compra recorrente, comprada com regularidade e nos mesmos termos.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "When teams price every order differently, the results become ___ and hard to audit."
items.why: Inconsistent = inconsistente: sem padrão, difícil de auditar.

items.q: "We only involve senior buyers with our strategic suppliers." These are suppliers who…
options: are important to the business and handled personally
are not yet on the approved list
items.why: Strategic supplier = fornecedor estratégico: os grandes e importantes, tratados de forma dedicada.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em reuniões de compras. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Finance still has to sign off on the framework agreement." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We plan to roll out the new supplier terms across all sites next quarter." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Two department heads pushed back on the standardised list." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar.

items.q: "The team agreed to renegotiate the freight rates but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Renegotiating a box of screws won't move the needle on our total spend." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = fazer diferença perceptível; aqui, não move o ponteiro do gasto total.
